ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2001, c 17, as amended; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184, as amended; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, Part XII.2; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1; Civil Code of Quebec, arts. 2186-2234 (particularly limited partnership rules); Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11. FINTRAC is the federal AML/CFT supervisor. Quebec's Registraire des entreprises maintains the enterprise register and mandatory disclosure of certain beneficial ownership information for enterprises dealing with public bodies.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in country of residence or Quebec notary; passport issued by competent national authority

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners against FINTRAC's Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) definitions, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Global Affairs Canada's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, and Canadian domestic sanctions regulations. Where any USD wire transfer is contemplated, OFAC SDN screening is mandatory to ensure compliance with U.S. sanctions and smooth clearing of SWIFT payments. Enhanced due diligence applies only if any party appears on a sanctions list, is a PEP, or if the transaction structure exhibits unexplained complexity. The financial intermediary and law firm must record screening dates, results, and evidence in the AML/KYC file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) online service — registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11) and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1), the limited partnership's name must be in French. A non-French name is permitted only where accompanied by a French name. Names must be written in Latin script; non-Latin scripts require a certified French transliteration. The name must include the distinctive legal element 'société en commandite' or the abbreviation 'S.E.C.' to denote limited partnership status. Common-law 'LP' may be used additionally but cannot replace the required French designation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Banking (federal financial institution approval required)
Assurance / Insurance / Assureur (authorization from Autorité des marchés financiers)
Université / University (prior approval from Ministère de l'Éducation)
Fiducie / Trust (authorization or regulated entity declaration required)
Canada / Canadien / National / Federal / Royal / Crown (official or Crown indicia requiring ministerial consent)
Commission / Société d'État / Agence publique (implies government mandate)
Montréal / Quebec / Ville de Montréal (geographic designations may require municipal or provincial authorization, and must not mislead as to location)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be renewed once for an additional 90 days by filing a renewal request and paying the applicable REQ fee before expiry. If the Registraire rejects the proposed name, the applicant may file a written administrative review within 30 days of the rejection notice, stating the legal and factual grounds and citing supporting registrations or trademarks. The REQ must reconsider and issue a written decision. If the review fails, the applicant may appeal judicially to the Court of Quebec (Civil Chamber) within 60 days of the review decision, pursuant to the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises and the Code of Civil Procedure. During the appeal window, no other identical name will be granted if a prior reservation remains in force.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is conditionally permissible for an ISIC 4791 low-risk B2B e-commerce limited partnership, provided the address is a staffed registered-office service in Quebec with physical reception capability, mail scanning, and statutory records custody. The address must be an 'établissement' under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises and must permit service of process and tax notices. A pure mail-forwarding virtual office without physical file retention or a professional Quebec representative is not recommended and may be rejected by the Registraire. The general partner must maintain a genuine place of management or a contractual agent with access to records.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low. For non-licensed electronic catalog retail, the expected probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the Registraire des entreprises or tax authorities in the first 12 months is approximately 2% to 5%, rising only upon red flags such as inconsistent declarations, tax non-filing, complaints, or unexplained high-volume cash or virtual-currency activity. Documentary and electronic checks are the primary supervision method.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CCQ), articles 2236–2261 (société en commandite); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, RLRQ c. P-44.1, sections 22 et seq. (registration of the initial declaration); Regulation respecting fees payable to the Registraire des entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Direction de l'immatriculation
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration initiale – société en commandite (Initial Declaration of a Limited Partnership) filed via the REQ online 'Registraire Central' service
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. Contributions are fixed by the partnership agreement; a limited partner may contribute money or property but not services under CCQ art. 2243. No escrow deposit is required and capital may be paid in instalments.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by the sole General Partner of the Limited Partnership, that: 1. The Partnership Agreement presented is hereby adopted, and the capital contributions of the general and limited partners are subscribed as set out in Schedule 'A'; 2. The registered office is fixed at [address], Province of Quebec, and the initial declaration shall be filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; 3. [Name] is appointed the General Partner, with exclusive authority to open banking accounts, execute declarations, and bind the partnership; 4. [Name] is appointed Operations Manager to obtain municipal, environmental, fire safety and occupational health licences. Adopted this ___ day of ____________, 2025.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Partnership Agreement Execution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online name-search service and Ministry of Justice notarial offices
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a distinctive name search through the REQ portal and obtain the name research report to establish legal distinctiveness. Execute the partnership agreement (contrat de société en commandite) identifying the general partner, limited partners, capital contributions, profit allocation, and management powers. If a partner contributes immovable property, the agreement must be notarized.
required_dossiers: Name research report (rapport de recherche de nom)
Partnership agreement (contrat de société en commandite)
Identification documents for each partner
Consent letters for the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for lack of distinctiveness or contravention, select a new distinctive element and resubmit the research; a rebuttal letter may be filed with the REQ within 30 days of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Initial Declaration and Payment of Registration Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Direction de l'immatriculation via online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Initial Declaration (Déclaration initiale – société en commandite) through the REQ online form, entering the partnership's French-language name, registered office, description of activities, partner details, and the signatory's authority. Pay the registration fee by credit card. Upon approval the REQ issues the attestation of registration and the NEQ number.
required_dossiers: Completed declaration form with authorized signature
Partnership agreement executed in step 1
Proof of registered office address in Québec
Fees covering the registration tariff
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any deficiencies noted by the REQ in the 'avis de défaut' and re-file the amended declaration online; engage the REQ mediation service if the refusal persists.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Business Number, GST/HST and QST Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online; Revenu Québec – Centre de services aux entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a Business Number (BN) account with the CRA and register for GST/HST where taxable supplies will exceed the $30,000 threshold or for voluntary registration. Register separately with Revenu Québec for QST and, if the partnership employs staff, for source deductions and the CNESST assessment. The general partner acts as the representative applicant for tax accounts.
required_dossiers: REQ attestation of registration (NEQ and legal entity details)
Partnership agreement allocating profits to partners
General partner's identification and authorization
Projected revenue statement for GST/HST registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Use the CRA 'My Business Account' and Revenu Québec 'clics affaires' portals to correct data; contact CRA Business Enquiries or the Revenu Québec tax account helpline for reconciliation of account numbers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Occupancy Permit and Commercial Establishment Licence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal permitting office (e.g., Ville de Montréal – Service de l'urbanisme et du développement économique; or local MRC inspection services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a commercial establishment operating permit and an occupancy certificate for the warehouse and administrative premises. Attach the lease, floor plans, and REQ registration attestation. The municipal inspector verifies zoning conformity, building standards, and fire safety. The permit is issued upon successful inspection and payment of local duties.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or ownership title
Architectural floor plans and site layout
REQ attestation of registration
Zoning compliance certificate
Fire prevention system description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Remediate inspection findings (fire exits, emergency lighting, structural deficiencies), submit corrected stamped plans, and reapply; municipal refusal may be appealed to the Tribunal administratif du Québec within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental Compliance Registration and Occupational Health Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MELCCFP – Direction générale de l'évaluation environnementale; CNESST – Direction de la prévention-inspection
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Assess whether the warehousing of MRO products (lubricants, batteries, solvents, chemical hardware) triggers section 22 of the Environment Quality Act. Where hazardous materials are stored above thresholds, file a Déclaration de conformité or application for a certificat d'autorisation through the MELCCFP online service. Register with CNESST if employees are engaged, and implement a written prevention program, first-aid stations, and a fire evacuation plan.
required_dossiers: Environmental self-assessment checklist and SDS documentation
Déclaration de conformité or certificat d'autorisation application (if applicable)
CNESST employer registration form and accident prevention plan
Fire safety inspection request and emergency measures plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to MELCCFP compliance notices within the stated delay and submit a corrective action plan; co-operate with CNESST inspectors to settle health and safety deficiencies before commercial operation commences.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal industrial permitting office (e.g., Ville de Montréal – Division des permis d'exploitation) with oversight of the Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE) for industrial policy; MELCCFP for environmental permits
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permis d'exploitation d'un établissement commercial (Commercial Establishment Operating Permit) with ancillary occupancy certificate

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) – Direction générale de l'évaluation environnementale
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III – Exempt/Registration: low-impact electronic catalogue retail and warehousing does not require a full Environmental Impact Assessment unless hazardous materials are stored above regulatory thresholds; otherwise a Déclaration de conformité under s. 22 of the Environment Quality Act and a supporting registre are required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Regulation respecting the quality of the atmosphere (VOC and particulate limits), municipal sewer discharge bylaws (BOD, TSS, pH), Regulation respecting hazardous residual materials for waste storage/disposal, and Code de sécurité du Québec for fuel storage tanks.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the municipal fire prevention service under the Quebec Fire Safety Code (RLRQ c. B-1.1, r. 8); structural load inspection certification for racking systems and mezzanine floors; CNESST occupational health and safety clearance comprising a first-aid plan, accident prevention program, and workplace inspection record under the Act respecting occupational health and safety (RLRQ c. S-2.1).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; portal: canada.ca/en/revenue-agency. For Quebec-specific QST, provincial tax returns, and provincial registration: Revenu Québec; portal: revenuquebec.ca.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity, including a non-resident limited partnership, must obtain a federal Business Number (BN) from the CRA, normally through the Business Registration Online (BRO) service using Form RC151 (or by mail where online access is unavailable). Registration for the GST/HST program account is mandatory once taxable supplies in Canada exceed CAD 30,000 in a rolling four-quarter period. For QST, registration with Revenu Québec is required under analogous small-supplier thresholds; the partnership must also obtain a Québec enterprise number (NEQ) through the Registraire des entreprises if it carries on business in Québec. No minimum capital or resident ownership condition applies to LP registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible (income-tax status as a fiscally transparent partnership; the LP itself does not pay federal/provincial income tax, but files an information return and allocates income to partners). For GST/HST and QST purposes, the partnership is treated as a separate registrant and must collect tax on taxable supplies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under Canadian federal or Québec income tax law. A limited partnership is transparent by statutory default; if all partners are Canadian residents it may qualify as a 'Canadian partnership' under Income Tax Act s.102(2). Hybrid-mismatch rules under ITA ss.12.7, 18.4-18.5, and 20(1) apply to cross-border arrangements involving hybrid entities. For indirect tax, the LP may voluntarily register for GST/HST and QST before exceeding the threshold and, once registered, has the usual elections for streamlined accounting and related-party supplies where applicable.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT-type goods and services tax: federal GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) plus Quebec QST (Quebec Sales Tax); no separate retail sales tax applies in Québec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (GST/HST threshold for small suppliers; the same CAD 30,000 threshold applies for QST under Revenu Québec rules).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API stamping, or pre-clearance e-invoice mandate in Canada or Québec. Invoicing is returns-based; commercial electronic invoices are accepted if they meet record-keeping standards. GST/HST returns must be filed electronically by registrants whose annual taxable supplies exceed CAD 1 million, and Revenu Québec requires electronic filing for applicable QST registrants. Records must be retained for six years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of industrial MRO goods may be zero-rated as an export under Excise Tax Act Part V of Schedule VI where the supplier ships or delivers the goods to a non-resident buyer outside Canada, possession and title pass outside Canada, and the goods are exported within the required period (generally within 60 days after the supply or within a longer period accepted by the CRA). The supplier must hold documentary commercial evidence of export and of the non-resident destination, including purchase orders, shipping records, and payment from the foreign buyer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A/CAED/eManifest export report filed with the Canada Border Services Agency)
Commercial invoice and packing list describing the goods and destination
Bill of lading / air waybill / carrier document proving physical export from Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank SWIFT/wire payment confirmation from the non-resident customer
Purchase order or sales contract with the non-resident buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec apply strict evidentiary tests before accepting zero-rating. If export documentation is missing or defective, the supply is recharacterized as taxable and the supplier is assessed for uncollected GST/HST and QST, with interest from the original remittance date and no offset for invoice underestimation. Penalties include false-statement penalties under Excise Tax Act s.285, gross-negligence penalties up to 50% of the net tax under s.285.1, and an extended reassessment period of up to seven years in circumstances of misrepresentation or neglect (ETA s.298). Revenu Québec may impose analogous QST penalties. Wilful evasion or fraudulent export zero-rating can lead to criminal prosecution under federal tax statutes.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada / Banque du Canada, with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) as prudential regulator; no dedicated foreign exchange administration exists, and the Minister of Finance and the Currency Act exercise residual authority over monetary and exchange-rate matters.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility under the IMF Article VIII framework. There are no general exchange controls, no surrender requirements, and no licensing or administrative authorization for routine foreign-currency transactions. The Canadian dollar is freely floating and deliverable in interbank markets. Profit remittances by a Quebec limited partnership to non-resident partners are permitted without Bank of Canada or AMF approval, but are subject to federal Part XIII withholding tax on deemed distributions to non-residents and to treaty-based rate reductions where applicable. The Investment Canada Act imposes a separate national-security and net-benefit review for certain foreign acquisitions of control, but this is not an FX control.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export-proceeds surrender rules in Canada. Exporters may retain foreign currency in authorized foreign-currency accounts at domestic or foreign banks without mandatory conversion timelines and there is no prescribed conversion ratio. Cross-border transaction reporting obligations arise only for statistical and AML purposes, principally through the Statistics Canada International Transactions Reporting System (ITRS) data collected by financial institutions and under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) or Canada Border Services Agency export reporting rules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: CAD/USD operating current account with segregated capital escrow sub-account
CAD/USD operating account plus non-interest-bearing escrow clearing sub-ledger
Capital escrow account and operational clearing account in CAD and USD
Merchant settlement operating account and capital injection escrow account
USD-denominated trade settlement account and CAD operating account
Quebec-headquartered consolidated operating and capital escrow account with US cross-border sweeps
Regional operating account for Quebec LP compliance with automated trust ledger capability

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-to-Medium for direct use of offshore digital EMIs as the sole treasury clearing institution. Under the Retail Payment Activities Act, any payment service provider serving Canadian end-users must register with the Bank of Canada and maintain prescribed safeguarding regimes; deposit-taking remains an exclusively Schedule I bank activity. An offshore EMI may be used for merchant acquiring or ancillary payment processing only through a registered Canadian PSP or in partnership with a Canadian chartered bank. Capital injection escrow, statutory settlement, and the core liquidity ledger must remain at an authorized Canadian bank or a wholly-owned foreign bank subsidiary in Canada. Quebec's Autorité des marchés financiers may also require provincial money-services-business registration in the event of remittance or currency-exchange services.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the PCMLTFA, Canadian banks are not statutorily required to hold an in-person board interview for a non-face-to-face corporate account opening when specified identity verification methods are used, including credit-bureau verification, government-issued photo ID, and registered-profile confirmation. For a Quebec registered limited partnership, the general partner or designated director and any beneficial owner owning 25% or more may ordinarily complete enhanced video KYC interviews with a designated client onboarding officer. Physical branch appearance is not mandated, but Canadian banks may require it as an internal risk decision when the LP has non-resident principals, complex partnership ownership, or incomplete corporate registers. For the highest onboarding certainty, the general partner's signing officer should be prepared to attend a Montreal office interview or complete a live video interview with a bank-accredited identity verifier.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership of the limited partnership, including general-partner layered ownership and indirect non-resident limited partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Official Quebec Registraire des entreprises LP attestation, full partnership agreement and certificate of limited partnership, current register of partners with identity and Canadian address, ultimate beneficial ownership statement identifying all 25% or greater partners and the control chain, notarized source-of-funds declarations for each capital contributor, and a corporate/ownership schematic signed by the general partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential exposure to sanctions, denied parties, or politically exposed persons in the trade counterparty base for industrial MRO e-commerce
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed bank sanctions and PEP questionnaire, third-party sanctions/denied-party screening reports covering the full supplier and customer base, end-user and end-use attestations, exports control classification for ISIC 4791 goods, and a written compliance policy declaring no dealings with sanctioned territories or listed parties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incoming international capital injection flagged as unusual or suspicious due to clearing through an offshore parent or non-Canadian funding source
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed limited partnership capital call and subscription documents, board resolution of the general partner approving the transfer, bank reference letter from the remitting institution, audited or reviewed financial statements or certified source-of-funds memorandum, and a notarized declaration of the business purpose tied to B2B e-commerce MRO inventory and working capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to reconcile projected trade volumes with banking requirements for merchant processing and SWIFT settlement in a cross-border catalog resale model
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed 12-month cash-flow forecast, sample commercial invoices and purchase orders from Canadian and U.S. industrial customers, supplier contracts evidencing commercial MRO procurement, logistics and customs brokerage agreements, and an AML/ATF institutional risk assessment showing Low_Risk_Standard classification for the e-commerce catalog model.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant route for inbound capital is a SWIFT MT103 international wire from the foreign parent or investor to the Quebec LP's CAD current account at a Schedule I Canadian bank. The beneficiary account must be in the legal name of the LP, and the wire instruction should include the phrase 'Limited Partnership Capital Contribution' in the payment details field to facilitate automatic ITRS classification, with the beneficiary bank's CIF code and the LP's Canadian business number. Banks will record the balance-of-payments purpose as direct investment equity in a Canadian enterprise; no FX approval is required, but the bank may request the capital call, partnership resolution, and closing balance sheet to substantiate the transaction. For U.S.-dollar injections retained for USD trade settlement, the financial institution may designate a USD domestic settlement account serviced through CIBC, RBC, or BMO U.S. branches, subject to the same source-of-funds documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border trade disbursements for industrial MRO procurement and settlement will use SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier payments and SWIFT MT202/MT202COV for correspondent-bank settlements where necessary. For large Canadian-dollar disbursements, the CAD priority payment will clear through the Bank of Canada Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or the modern Real-Time Rail for retail transactions; USD trade payments may traverse bank-owned U.S. clearing networks using the Canadian bank's U.S. dollar clearing account. Commercial letters of credit for recurring supplier financing should be issued through the Canadian account bank's trade desk in Montreal or Toronto, advised and confirmed through the beneficiary's bank, with documents compliant under UCP 600. Merchant receipts from B2B MRO e-commerce card payments settle separately through the Canadian bank's merchant acquiring or a registered PSP, with the collected funds swept into the LP operating ledger.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable over-the-counter USD/CAD forward contracts with a Canadian Schedule I bank under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or long-form FX confirmation
FX swaps for temporary USD/CAD principal exchange covering inventory-cycle cash needs
Cross-currency swaps (USD/CAD fixed-for-fixed or floating-for-floating) where trade receivables and payables maturity mismatches exceed one year
Window forwards and flexible forward contracts for rolling MRO procurement payments
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for settlement exposure in emerging-market currencies of offshore suppliers, subject to bank credit limits and Canada AML/ATF sanctions screening

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) with beneficial ownership confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each registration anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalty of CAD 210 per infraction; persistent non-filing leads to administrative strike-off or dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 5 months after fiscal period end (May 31 for calendar-year partnerships)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty: CAD 25 per day, up to CAD 2,500 per return; additional penalties for gross negligence or repeated non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Relevé 15 (RL-15) and summary for Quebec partners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Last day of February following the calendar year in which the fiscal period ends (February 28 for December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty: CAD 25 per day per slip, up to CAD 2,500; administrative interest may apply.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is mandatory for a limited partnership in Quebec; audit becomes compulsory only if the partnership agreement, creditor, or securities legislation requires (e.g., publicly accountable issuer).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: ASPE (applicable to Canadian private enterprises) or IFRS if publicly accountable; tax-basis adjustments applied for CRA and Revenu Québec reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The REQ annual declaration must identify all ultimate beneficial owners and confirm their details; any change in partners or UBO within the year triggers an amending declaration (déclaration modificative) within 30 days.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined general corporate rate for a corporate partner (15% federal Part I + 11.5% Quebec corporate rate). The Quebec Limited Partnership itself is fiscally transparent and is not subject to corporate income tax; income is allocated to partners and taxed at the partner level.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sectoral tax holiday applies to electronic catalogue MRO distribution. A Canadian-controlled private corporate partner qualifying for the federal small business deduction and Quebec small business deduction can reduce the combined effective rate to approximately 12.2% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income. Federal investment tax credits for qualified manufacturing/processing property and SR&ED credits, plus Quebec innovation tax credits, may reduce effective tax if the MRO operator develops proprietary e-commerce software or warehouse automation technology.
